Onboarding.skill_q1_question: What happens when you 'buy' Bitcoin on an exchange like Binance?
Onboarding.skill_q1_option_a: You receive physical Bitcoin in your wallet
Onboarding.skill_q1_option_b: The exchange holds the Bitcoin for you (custody)
Onboarding.skill_q1_option_c: Bitcoin is printed specifically for you
Onboarding.skill_q1_option_d: You become a partial owner of Binance
Onboarding.skill_q1_explanation: When you buy on an exchange, they hold the Bitcoin for you. You only have a credit. 'Not your keys, not your coins' - if the exchange fails, you risk losing everything.
Onboarding.skill_q2_question: Why does Bitcoin have a limit of 21 million coins?
Onboarding.skill_q2_option_a: It's a magic number chosen by Satoshi
Onboarding.skill_q2_option_b: To create artificial scarcity and drive up price
Onboarding.skill_q2_option_c: To prevent inflation and maintain value over time
Onboarding.skill_q2_option_d: Because 21 million is the maximum the technology can handle
Onboarding.skill_q2_explanation: The limit serves to prevent inflation. Unlike traditional currencies that can be printed infinitely, Bitcoin has a fixed and predictable monetary policy.
Onboarding.skill_q3_question: What does 'DeFi' mean and why is it different from traditional banks?
Onboarding.skill_q3_option_a: Decentralized Finance - uses smart contracts instead of banks
Onboarding.skill_q3_option_b: Digital Finance - it's just the online version of banks
Onboarding.skill_q3_option_c: Definitive Finance - it's the final evolution of money
Onboarding.skill_q3_option_d: Democratic Finance - everyone can vote on interest rates
Onboarding.skill_q3_explanation: DeFi uses smart contracts on blockchain to create financial services without intermediaries. Instead of trusting a bank, you trust code (which is public and verifiable).
